{{Short description|American mathematician (1938–2019)}}
'''David F. Shanno''' (born April 19, 1938 – 2019<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.informs.org/Explore/History-of-O.R.-Excellence/Biographical-Profiles/Shanno-David |title=David Shanno |publisher=www.informs.org |date= |accessdate=2017-08-26}}</ref>) was an American mathematician, who specialized in [[mathematical optimization]] and [[operations research]]. He was professor emeritus at [[Rutgers University]] (Rutgers Center for Operations Research, Rutcor).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rutcor.rutgers.edu/~shanno/vita.html |title=Curriculum Vitae David F. Shanno |publisher=rutcor.rutgers.edu |date= |accessdate=2017-08-26 |archive-date=2016-03-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160319084830/http://rutcor.rutgers.edu/~shanno/vita.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Shanno obtained his B.Sc. in mathematics from [[Yale University]] in 1959, his M.Sc. in mathematics from [[Carnegie-Mellon University]] 1962, and his Ph.D. in 1967. He held positions at the [[University of Chicago]], the [[University of Toronto]], the [[University of Arizona]] and the [[University of California, Davis]] before becoming professor at Rutgers University.

In 1970 he was one of the developers of the [[Broyden–Fletcher–Goldfarb–Shanno algorithm|BFGS algorithm]], a [[Quasi-Newton method]].<ref>Shanno ''Conditioning of quasi-Newton methods for function minimization'', Math. Computation, Band 24, 1970, S. 647-656, Shanno, Paul Kettler ''Optimal conditioning of quasi-Newton methods'', ibid. 657-664</ref>

In 2005 he became a fellow at [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences|INFORMS]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Fellows/INFORMS-Fellows-Class-of-2005 |title=INFORMS Fellows: Class of 2005 |publisher=www.informs.org |date= |accessdate=2017-08-26}}</ref> He received the E.M.L. Beale – W.B. Orchard-Hayes Prize for Excellence in Computational Mathematical Programming of the [[Mathematical Programming Society]] in 1991 together with I. J. Lustig and R. E. Marsten. Shanno was associate editor of the journal ''Mathematical Programming'' from 1980 to 1989 and of the ''Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications'' from 1982 to 1990.
